items.summary: A Fox News Digital report frames SpaceX as facing rising political risk in the United States, where Democrats are preparing to take control of Congress. The company reportedly hired five experienced lobbyists from Washington DC lobbying firm Mehlman Consulting, several with ties to prominent Democratic Party leaders and the previous administration; their effective registration is set for October 1. Potential investigations cited by Democratic lawmakers include limiting Ukraine's satellite communication services, US defense dependence on SpaceX, and possible conflicts of interest between Musk and the Trump administration. The report notes SpaceX's estimated value at around $2 trillion across aerospace engineering, AI, telecommunications, and space transportation, warning that a sharp decline could affect the broader economy. Separately, it reports Musk distancing himself from MAGA politics after a New York Times summit where he said he is not 'MAGA,' expressing disappointment over spending large sums on elections without notable results. The article also states Palantir has similarly hired Democratic-aligned lobbyists; AI Now Institute senior fellow and former Biden administration official Ayat Ibrahim told NPR that big tech companies have substantial resources and will try to spend them across different venues to avoid accountability. Finally, it reports a sharp decline in technology stocks after Democrats' midterm election win, with particular pressure on AI infrastructure and data center firms amid investor fears of stricter regulation under new political conditions.
items.title: SpaceX hires five lobbyists amid Democratic scrutiny and political pressure

items.summary: The Guardian reported that former NFL quarterback Tom Brady is pursuing a minority stake at Stamford Bridge, with Alex Spiro of the New York firm Quinn Emanuel joining him by investing through Chelsea's majority owners, Clearlake Capital. Both would become limited partners holding no voting rights if their deals complete. This follows Clearlake's September agreement to buy out Todd Boehly and Mark Walter for around £1bn — a deal due to close year-end — after which Clearlake will own 86.5% of Chelsea; the two sellers each held 12.9%, while Hansjorg Wyss retained his position by buying 12.9% of Clearlake's shareholding, and Brady's and Spiro's investments are understood to be considerably smaller than those amounts. Spiro has represented Musk since 2018 and advised on his $44bn (£33.6bn) acquisition of Twitter in 2022; he also defended Musk in a 2019 defamation trial, helped Alec Baldwin's acquittal in 2024, and represents Joshua Kushner over the latter's legal challenge to Uefa regarding Gianni Infantino's $4.2bn World Cup scheme. Brady previously held a 3.3% stake in Birmingham City until this month — which sources said he was selling to make way for his Chelsea investment — having bought into that club in August 2023 after Knighthead Capital's takeover, and also owns a minority stake in the Las Vegas Raiders; he has a relationship with Clearlake power broker Behdad Eghbali. Chelsea declined to comment.
items.title: Tom Brady and Elon Musk's lawyer join Clearlake as minority investors in Chelsea
